title_en: Beijing Bochuang Yingnuowei Technology Co., Ltd. v. Poly Civil Explosives Technology Group Co., Ltd. — contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: Export tax rebate is a measure adopted by China to encourage exports. In this case, there is no situation of fake exports without actual goods being exported, so the exporter is entitled to receive the export tax rebate. The foreign trade agency contract involved in this case contains a clause providing that the export tax rebate shall be paid by the foreign trade agent to the principal. This clause is an agreement between the parties on the redistribution of the export tax rebate, and constitutes a disposition of rights by the parties based on their true intentions. Therefore, the contract should not be deemed as a contract entered into for the illegal purpose of defrauding the state of export tax rebates, and should not be held invalid. The export tax rebate obtained by the foreign trade agent shall be paid to the principal in accordance with the contract.

full_text_en:
北京博创英诺威科技有限公司与保利民爆科技集团股份有限公司合同纠纷案

Beijing Bochuang Innove Technology Co., Ltd. v. Poly Minbao Technology Group Co., Ltd. — contract dispute

【裁判摘要】

[Ruling Summary]

Export tax rebates are measures adopted by China to encourage export. In this case, there is no circumstance of falsely claiming export without actual genuine export of goods, and the exporter is entitled to obtain export tax rebates. The foreign trade agency contract involved in this case stipulated a clause that the export tax rebates shall be paid by the foreign trade agent to the principal. This clause is an agreement between the parties regarding the redistribution of export tax rebates, and is a disposal of rights by the parties based on their genuine intent. The contract should not be deemed invalid on the ground that it was concluded for the illegal purpose of defrauding the state of export tax rebates. The foreign trade agent shall pay the export tax rebates it obtained to the principal in accordance with the contract.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2013) Min Ti Zi No. 73

Reconsideration Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Beijing Bochuang Innove Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 2, Building 2, Yard 11, Xiaoying North Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Lu Pingjian, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Yingyang, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yuan Wei, Attorney at Beijing Jincheng Tongda & Neal Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Poly Minbao Technology Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Yard A11, Anxiang Beili, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Chen Xiaozhong, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Meng, Attorney at Beijing V&T Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ma Jing, Attorney at Beijing V&T Law Firm.

The Reconsideration Applicant, Beijing Bochuang Innove Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bochuang Company), filed a request for reconsideration with this Court against the civil judgment (2011) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 854 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court on April 20, 2012, in a dispute over a contract with the Respondent, Poly Minbao Technology Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minbao Company). Upon review, this Court issued the civil ruling (2012) Min Shen Zi No. 889 on March 20, 2013, ordering that this case be retried by this Court. After the retrial was granted, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on July 19, 2013. The authorized representatives of the Reconsideration Applicant, Bochuang Company, Zhu Yingyang and Yuan Wei, and the authorized representatives of the Respondent, Minbao Company, Xu Meng and Ma Jing, all appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Bochuang Company filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, alleging: In September 2006, Bochuang Company reached an intention with the foreign company Redcliffe Holdings Limited to export three sets of ZJ50 low-temperature drilling rigs and related auxiliary system equipment (including spare parts). In the same month, Bochuang Company issued a tender notice and organized a bidding process, ultimately selecting seven domestic manufacturers as winning bidders to become the drilling rig manufacturers. Between October and November of the same year, Bochuang Company organized negotiations between the foreign company and the manufacturers regarding the order content. Thereafter, Bochuang Company selected Minbao Company as the export company for the above project, and entrusted Minbao Company to sign export product procurement contracts with the domestic equipment manufacturers and a sales contract for the batch of equipment with the foreign company. On December 1, 2006, Bochuang Company and Minbao Company signed the "Cooperation Agreement," in which the parties agreed on the following income distribution method: Minbao Company would charge 0.6% of the total sales contract amount as a project management fee. After each receipt of foreign exchange remittance from the foreign company and completion of bank settlement, Minbao Company would pay the factory the corresponding payment according to the export product procurement contract requirements, deduct Minbao Company's corresponding management fee and related business expenses, and pay the remaining amount in full to Bochuang Company. It was also agreed that Minbao Company must pay all export tax rebates to Bochuang Company within five working days after receiving the project export tax rebates. After the "Cooperation Agreement" was signed, Bochuang Company performed its obligations as agreed, negotiating and finalizing the terms of the sales contract and the export product procurement contract with the foreign company and the manufacturers. On the 20th of the same month, under the arrangement of Bochuang Company, Minbao Company signed a sales contract with the foreign company, with a total amount of USD 39,316,890. In the same month, Minbao Company signed export product procurement contracts with domestic manufacturers including Shanghai Shenkai Petroleum Chemical Equipment Co., Ltd. During the project execution, Bochuang Company performed its corresponding obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement," including supervising the manufacturing of various components and complete machines of the export equipment, arranging for the foreign company to inspect and accept the equipment, training the foreign company's operators, and bearing all expenses required for export performance, including domestic and international transportation, insurance, freight and miscellaneous charges, loading and unloading, storage, inspection, custody, bank handling fees, and performing the obligations of joint commissioning of the three drilling rigs and on-site installation abroad. In the early stage of project execution, Bochuang Company and Minbao Company had a good cooperative relationship and performed their respective obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement." However, after Minbao Company replaced its general manager in April 2008, Minbao Company refused to perform its payment obligations to Bochuang Company, and the cooperative relationship between the parties gradually deteriorated. Currently, the above foreign trade contracts, export product procurement contracts, and spare parts contracts have all been performed. The foreign company paid Minbao Company a total of USD 39,344,051.50 (settled at the prevailing exchange rate into RMB 295,019,149.73), and Minbao Company paid a total of RMB 275,560,197.04 to the domestic suppliers. The price difference between the sales contract and the export product procurement contracts was RMB 19,458,952.69. According to the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by the parties, Minbao Company was entitled to a management fee of RMB 1,677,194, project stamp duty of RMB 5,181.94, and handling fees of RMB 1,645.15. After deducting these fees, the remaining price difference of RMB 17,774,931.60 should be paid in full by Minbao Company to Bochuang Company. However, as of April 2008, Minbao Company had only paid Bochuang Company RMB 6,000,000 and paid transportation and other expenses of RMB 1,661,811.54 as instructed by Bochuang Company, and still owed Bochuang Company RMB 10,113,120.06. In addition, according to the "Cooperation Agreement," Minbao Company had not paid a single cent of the export tax rebates of over RMB 38,000,000 that it was required to pay. Bochuang Company repeatedly demanded payment of the above arrears, but Minbao Company refused to pay. Therefore, Bochuang Company requested the court to order: 1. Minbao Company to pay Bochuang Company the contract arrears of RMB 10,113,120.06; 2. Minbao Company to pay Bochuang Company interest for overdue payment from April 16, 2008, to the date of performance specified in the judgment (calculated to November 16, 2009, as RMB 991,747.97, based on the principal of RMB 10,113,120.06, at the one-to-three-year loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period); 3. Minbao Company to pay Bochuang Company the export tax rebates it received, amounting to RMB 38,656,941.56; 4. Minbao Company to pay Bochuang Company the attorney's fees of RMB 700,000 for this case.

The court of first instance found: On December 1, 2006, Minbao Company (Party A, at that time named New Times Minbao Technology Co., Ltd., changed to New Times Minbao Technology Group Co., Ltd. in January 2009, and changed to the current name during the litigation of this case) and Bochuang Company (Party B) signed the "Cooperation Agreement" (Agreement No.: MB-DRS-0612), agreeing to cooperate in exporting three sets of ZJ50 drilling rigs and related auxiliary system equipment to the foreign company Redcliffe Holdings Limited. Article 1 of the agreement specified 15 contracts and their contract numbers, including foreign trade contracts, domestic procurement contracts, and transportation contracts. Article 2 of the agreement, "Rights and Obligations of Both Parties," clearly stipulated: "1. Party A's rights and obligations: (1) Sign and execute the above foreign trade contracts and domestic procurement contracts, which shall directly bind Party B and the foreign company, and Party B and the domestic suppliers. (2) Handle procedures for export customs declaration, transportation, etc., on behalf of Party B as instructed. (3) Handle financial settlement of payments with domestic suppliers on behalf of Party B as instructed. (4) Handle export tax rebate procedures on behalf of Party B as instructed… 2. Party B's rights and obligations: (1) Bear all expenses required for export performance, including domestic and international transportation, insurance, freight and miscellaneous charges, loading and unloading, storage, inspection, customs declaration, bank handling fees. (2) Perform various obligations agreed with the foreign company. (3) Be responsible for project information collection, preliminary project contacts, liaison with suppliers, ensuring that manufacturers and service providers execute relevant product and service contracts, and ensuring that quantity, specifications, quality, packaging, delivery time, etc., comply with the foreign company's requirements and the foreign trade contract provisions. (4) Be responsible for contacting and negotiating with the foreign company on relevant matters, investigating its creditworthiness on its own. If the foreign company delays contract performance or fails to pay on time, causing payment disputes between Party A and domestic suppliers, Party B shall ultimately perform all obligations, including payment obligations, agreed by Party A in the contracts signed with domestic suppliers. (5) If the actual shipped goods do not conform to the description of the goods in the foreign trade contract, resulting in false customs declarations and violation of relevant national laws and regulations, Party B shall bear full responsibility. (6) Be responsible for the supervision of the manufacture of the export equipment under the contract." Article 3 of the agreement, "Income Distribution," stipulated: "1. Total amount of the foreign trade contract: USD 39,316,890. 2. Party A's domestic procurement payment shall be based on the actual amount of the domestic trade contract received. 3. Party A shall charge Party B 0.6% of the total amount of the foreign trade contract as a management fee for the project. Party B clarifies that Party A is not required to advance funds under this contract. If Party A needs to advance funds under the domestic and foreign trade contracts, the parties will separately discuss the management fee. 4. After each receipt of foreign exchange remittance from the foreign party and completion of bank settlement, Party A shall pay the factory the corresponding payment according to the domestic procurement contract requirements, and after deducting Party A's corresponding management fee and related business expenses, the remaining amount shall be paid by Party A to Party B or the payee designated by Party B within five banking days in the manner designated by Party B… 5. Party A agrees that upon receipt of the export tax rebates under Contract No. MBIE0611RIGA1, it shall pay all tax rebates to Party B within five banking days. Payment shall be deemed to have been made once Party A makes payment from its bank account…"

From December 7, 2006, Minbao Company successively signed a series of export product procurement contracts with domestic manufacturers. On December 2, 2006, regarding the export of three drilling rigs and related auxiliary systems and parts, Minbao Company signed a sales contract with the foreign company Redcliffe Holdings Limited. All of the above contracts have been performed. The foreign company paid Minbao Company a total of USD 39,344,051.50 (settled at the prevailing exchange rate into RMB 295,019,149.73), and Minbao Company paid a total of RMB 275,560,197.04 to the domestic suppliers. In February 2007, Minbao Company paid transportation fees of RMB 1,260,200 to China Railway Foreign Service International Freight Forwarding Co., Ltd.

On March 15, 2007, Minbao Company (Party A) and Bochuang Company (Party B) signed the "Service Contract," which stipulated: 1. Party A entrusts Party B to be responsible for technical services such as design modifications, supervision of manufacture, and technical support for the petroleum drilling rigs and related drilling systems under the foreign trade contract (No. MBIE0611RIGA1) signed by Party A with the foreign company. 2. Party B's responsibilities and scope of work are detailed in Annex A of this contract. 3. Based on the client's requirements raised at the Baoji meeting on January 20, 2007, regarding modifications to the drilling rig's moving track and its control system, Party B is specifically entrusted to redesign and supervise the manufacture of the moving tracks and control systems for the three drilling rigs. 4. Party A and Party B, after negotiation, determine that Party B's fee for completing the above work is RMB 9,750,000. The above fee is a full lump-sum fee. If Party B's expenses exceed the above amount, Party A will not be responsible for additional compensation… 6. If any disagreement arises between the parties regarding the above terms or matters not covered by this contract, the parties shall resolve them through negotiation and sign a supplementary agreement to confirm the negotiation results, which shall have the same legal effect as this contract. After the "Service Contract" was signed, Minbao Company successively paid Bochuang Company technical consultation fees of RMB 6,000,000.

On April 25, 2007, Minbao Company (Party A) and Bochuang Company (Party B) signed the "Supplementary Agreement," which stated: According to the "Cooperation Agreement" (Agreement No.: MB-DRS-0612) signed by both parties, Party A shall pay Party B under the "Cooperation Agreement" after the corresponding matters are completed; currently, the foreign party has paid four installments to Party A under the foreign trade contract, but due to the supervision of these funds by China Minsheng Bank, they cannot be paid to Party B. After negotiation, both parties agree that Party A will prepay RMB 2,000,000 from its own account to Party B to alleviate Party B's capital turnover difficulties; after the release of the supervised funds by China Minsheng Bank, according to the relevant provisions of the agreement (Agreement No.: MB-DRS-0612) signed by both parties, Party A will deduct RMB 2,000,000 from the remaining contract amount to be settled with Party B; this "Supplementary Agreement" has the same legal effect as the "Cooperation Agreement."

Regarding the performance of the "Cooperation Agreement" in this case, Bochuang Company submitted to the court of first instance emails exchanged with the foreign company and domestic petroleum drilling rig manufacturers from September to December 2006, to prove that it had contacted the foreign company to reach an intention to buy and sell petroleum drilling rig equipment, selected seven domestic petroleum drilling rig manufacturers through bidding, organized technical clarification meetings with the foreign company and manufacturers to finalize the overall technical plan and requirements for the drilling rigs, and organized business meetings with domestic manufacturers to finalize the drilling rig order content. Minbao Company stated that it could not confirm the authenticity and relevance of the above emails, but did not provide corresponding evidence to prove that it had independently contacted the foreign company and domestic petroleum drilling rig manufacturers regarding the export business in this case.

Regarding the first claim, Bochuang Company claimed that under the "Cooperation Agreement," the arrears payable by Minbao Company to it amounted to RMB 10,113,120.06, calculated as the total amount of the sales contract of RMB 295,019,149.73 minus various payments already made. The payments already made included: the payable payment for the export product procurement contracts of RMB 275,560,197.04, expenses paid of RMB 7,661,811.54, Minbao Company's project management fee payable of RMB 1,677,194, export handling fees of RMB 1,645.15, and stamp duty of RMB 5,181.94. Bochuang Company did not provide the relevant vouchers for the above expenses paid and handling fees and stamp duty, and Minbao Company also did not acknowledge them. Minbao Company, on the other hand, claimed that it had incurred the following expenses for the export business in this case: Bochuang Company's service fee of RMB 9,750,000 (of which RMB 2,489,800 was unpaid), personnel-related expenses of RMB 650,327.67, 2008 income tax of RMB 4,090,584.77, stamp duty of RMB 172,271.48, guarantee letter handling fees of RMB 199,840.06, bank handling fees of RMB 4,488.32, and office expenses, meeting expenses, travel expenses, and entertainment expenses of RMB 211,933.65, totaling RMB 15,079,445.95. Among these, Minbao Company provided a list prepared unilaterally to prove its personnel-related expenses, office expenses, meeting expenses, travel expenses, and entertainment expenses. Bochuang Company did not acknowledge the relevance of the above personnel-related expenses, 2008 income tax, office expenses, meeting expenses, travel expenses, and entertainment expenses claimed by Minbao Company to the export business in this case.

Upon application by Bochuang Company, the court of first instance, during the first instance trial, investigated with the Import and Export Tax Management Section of the Chaoyang District State Taxation Bureau of Beijing, and found that Minbao Company had obtained a total of RMB 38,458,237.51 in export tax rebates based on the export business in this case.

The court of first instance held:

I. Regarding the validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" in this case. Minbao Company argued that the contract fell within the circumstances described in Article 2 of the "Notice on Further Regulating the Order of Foreign Trade Export and Effectively Strengthening the Administration of Export Goods Tax Rebates (Exemptions)" issued by the State Administration of Taxation and the Ministry of Commerce of China, namely, "an export enterprise exports under its own name, but the export business is essentially completed by operators other than the enterprise and its invested enterprises under the guise of the export enterprise's name," and therefore the contract was a contract that concealed the illegal purpose of fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates under a legal form, and thus should be deemed invalid. Based on the facts found, the export business in this case existed in reality, Minbao Company actually participated in the entire process of the export business in this case, and the sales contract it signed with the foreign company and the export product procurement contracts it signed with the domestic manufacturers had all been performed. The export business in this case was not completed by Bochuang Company under the guise of Minbao Company's name, nor was there any illegal circumstance of defrauding the state of export tax rebates. Therefore, Minbao Company's defense was unfounded, and the "Cooperation Agreement" in this case should be held valid.

II. Regarding the performance of the "Cooperation Agreement" in this case. Minbao Company claimed that the export business in this case was completed by it independently and submitted as evidence the sales contract it signed with the foreign company, the export product procurement contracts it signed with the domestic manufacturers, and the advance payment guarantee letter it provided to the foreign buyer. First, signing and executing the sales contracts and domestic procurement contracts for the export products and providing advance payment guarantees to the foreign buyer were all obligations Minbao Company should perform under the "Cooperation Agreement." Second, Bochuang Company submitted a large number of emails to prove that it had performed its obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement," including preliminary project contact, liaison with the foreign company and suppliers. Although Minbao Company did not acknowledge the authenticity and relevance of the above emails, it did not provide contrary evidence to refute them. Based on the principle of preponderance of evidence, it should be determined that the "Cooperation Agreement" had been actually performed. Minbao Company claimed that the "Cooperation Agreement" in this case had been replaced by the later "Service Contract" signed by the parties. First, from the content of the "Service Contract," there was no expression of intent to replace the "Cooperation Agreement." Second, the "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties on April 25, 2007, to solve the capital turnover problem stated that the "Supplementary Agreement" had the same legal effect as the "Cooperation Agreement." Furthermore, according to the "Cooperation Agreement," Minbao Company was responsible for the supervision of the manufacture of the export equipment under the contract, so it should be determined that the signing and performance of the "Service Contract" constituted acts of the parties in performing the "Cooperation Agreement." Therefore, Minbao Company's defense was also not accepted.

III. Regarding the Claims of Bochuang Company in This Case. The "Cooperation Agreement" in this case is legally valid and binding on both parties. The export business in this case has been fully performed. Bochuang Company has adduced evidence to prove that it performed its relevant obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement" as agreed, and Minbao Company should also pay the corresponding amounts to Bochuang Company as agreed. According to the "Cooperation Agreement," after each receipt of foreign remittance and completion of bank settlement, Minbao Company shall pay the corresponding payment to the factory according to the domestic procurement contract requirements, deduct the management fee due to Party A and relevant business expenses, and pay the remaining balance to Bochuang Company within five banking working days. In the export business of this case, the foreign party paid a total equivalent to RMB 295,019,149.73 to Minbao Company, and Minbao Company paid a total of RMB 275,560,197.04 to domestic suppliers. The project management fee payable by Bochuang Company to Minbao Company, according to the "Cooperation Agreement," should be 0.6% of the total foreign trade contract amount of RMB 295,019,149.73, i.e., RMB 1,770,114.90. Regarding the relevant business expenses to be deducted, since Bochuang Company did not provide vouchers for the expenditure of the relevant expenses, they shall be determined based on the expenses proved by Minbao Company's evidence, including: paid technical consulting fees of RMB 6,000,000, freight charges of RMB 1,260,200, stamp duty of RMB 172,271.48, guarantee handling fees of RMB 199,840.06, and bank handling fees of RMB 4,488.32. Regarding Minbao Company's claim for personnel expenses of RMB 650,327.67 and office expenses, meeting expenses, travel expenses, and entertainment expenses of RMB 211,933.65 incurred for the export business in this case, the detailed list unilaterally prepared by it lacks relevance to this case. However, considering that Minbao Company inevitably incurred the above-mentioned expenses to complete the export business, this part of the expenses is determined by discretion to be RMB 200,000. Minbao Company also claimed to deduct its 2008 income tax of RMB 4,090,584.77, which is not supported due to lack of contractual basis. In summary, after deducting various expenses, the remaining balance of the export project that Minbao Company should pay to Bochuang Company is RMB 9,852,037.93.

Regarding Bochuang Company's request for Minbao Company to pay overdue interest on the above amount. Since the agreement did not clearly stipulate the payment date, and both parties failed to adduce evidence within the evidence submission period to prove the specific date on which the export business in this case was actually fully performed, this request is partially supported. That is, from the date Bochuang Company filed the lawsuit until the expiration of the performance period specified in the judgment, based on the payable remaining project balance of RMB 9,852,037.93, interest shall be calculated at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period.

Regarding Bochuang Company's claim for Minbao Company to pay the export tax refund. In this case, Minbao Company, as a self-operating export enterprise, actually completed the trade under the export contract and obtained the export tax refund, which complies with the relevant national export tax refund system regulations. Minbao Company voluntarily agreed in the "Cooperation Agreement" with Bochuang Company to pay the export tax refund obtained under the export contract of this case to Bochuang Company. This constitutes a disposition of its own property and does not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws and administrative regulations. Considering Minbao Company's defense argument regarding the imbalance of interests between the contracting parties, and the labor contributed by Minbao Company to complete the export business of this case, based on the principle of fairness, it is determined by discretion to deduct RMB 1,800,000 from the total export tax refund amount as remuneration for Minbao Company's services, and the remaining amount shall be paid by Minbao Company to Bochuang Company.

Regarding Bochuang Company's request for Minbao Company to pay the attorney's fees of RMB 700,000 in this case, it lacks a contractual basis and is not supported.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 8 and 61 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered Civil Judgment (2010) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 1940:

1. Minbao Company shall pay Bochuang Company the remaining balance of the export project of RMB 9,852,037.93 within ten days after the judgment takes effect.

2. Minbao Company shall pay Bochuang Company overdue interest (interest from December 25, 2000, to the expiration of the performance period specified in the judgment, based on RMB 9,852,037.93, calculated at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period) within ten days after the judgment takes effect.

3. Minbao Company shall pay Bochuang Company RMB 36,658,237.51 within ten days after the judgment takes effect.

4. Bochuang Company's other claims are dismissed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 294,109 shall be borne by Bochuang Company in the amount of RMB 19,758 and by Minbao Company in the amount of RMB 274,351.

Minbao Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court.

During the second-instance trial, the court of second instance, in early June 2011, sent a letter to the State Administration of Taxation seeking its opinion on the characterization of the "Cooperation Agreement" and corresponding facts involved in this case. The State Administration of Taxation replied on the 24th of the same month: "According to the 'Cooperation Agreement' provided by your court... this export business is essentially not operated by Minbao Company. If this 'Cooperation Agreement' is executed, it falls under the circumstances described in Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the 'Notice of the State Administration of Taxation and the Ministry of Commerce on Further Standardizing the Order of Foreign Trade Export Operations and Effectively Strengthening the Administration of Export Goods Tax Rebates (Exemptions)' (Guo Shui Fa [2006] No. 24), namely: an export enterprise exports in its own name, but the export business is essentially completed by other operators (or enterprises, individual operators, or other individuals) other than the enterprise and its invested enterprises, using the export enterprise's name. According to Articles 2 and 3 of Guo Shui Fa [2006] No. 24, for such export businesses, the export enterprise shall not apply to the tax authorities for export goods tax rebates (exemptions). If tax rebates (exemptions) have already been declared, the rebated (exempted) tax shall be recovered; tax not yet rebated (exempted) shall no longer be processed."

The court of second instance held that: The lawful formation of a civil contract not only requires full civil capacity and genuine expression of intent but also requires that the form and content of the contract comply with laws and regulations. The "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Minbao Company and Bochuang Company on December 1, 2006, was based on the true expression of intent of both parties at the time and had already performed most of the contractual obligations except for the payment obligation. As a dispute over contractual interests arose between the parties, the validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" has become the key issue in this case. This should include two aspects.

First, the output of benefits damages the legitimate rights and interests of state-owned assets. It is not difficult to see from the "Cooperation Agreement" and its actual performance that Minbao Company, as a state-controlled foreign trade enterprise, its own good credit status was a reliable guarantee fully trusted by the domestic and foreign trade enterprises in this case, and it therefore assumed all contractual risks and responsibilities in the domestic and foreign trade contracts in this case. However, according to the "Cooperation Agreement," Minbao Company's profit was merely a management fee of 0.6% of the contract amount, which was disproportionate to the huge contractual risks it assumed. The vast majority of the profits from the domestic and foreign trade contracts were allocated to Bochuang Company. Such a significant output of benefits inevitably damages the legitimate interests of state-controlled enterprises. Therefore, the contractual purpose of the "Cooperation Agreement" regarding the output of benefits from state-owned assets is illegal.

Second, export tax rebates shall not be obtained illegally. Export tax rebates are an important way for the state to promote foreign trade. Article 34 of the Foreign Trade Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates that acts of fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates are prohibited in foreign trade activities. Fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates is obviously illegal. Article 38, Paragraph 3 of the Implementing Rules of the Tax Collection Administration Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that tax authorities shall strengthen the administration of export tax rebates for taxpayers, and the specific administrative measures shall be formulated by the State Administration of Taxation together with the relevant departments of the State Council. In view of this, the court sent a letter to the State Administration of Taxation seeking its opinion on the characterization of the "Cooperation Agreement" under this case. The State Administration of Taxation clearly stated: "This export business is essentially not operated by Minbao Company. If this 'Cooperation Agreement' is executed, it falls under the circumstances described in Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the 'Notice of the State Administration of Taxation and the Ministry of Commerce on Further Standardizing the Order of Foreign Trade Export Operations and Effectively Strengthening the Administration of Export Goods Tax Rebates (Exemptions)' (Guo Shui Fa [2006] No. 24), namely: an export enterprise exports in its own name, but the export business is essentially completed by other operators (or enterprises, individual operators, or other individuals) other than the enterprise and its invested enterprises, using the export enterprise's name. According to Articles 2 and 3 of Guo Shui Fa [2006] No. 24, for such export businesses, the export enterprise shall not apply to the tax authorities for export goods tax rebates (exemptions). If tax rebates (exemptions) have already been declared, the rebated (exempted) tax shall be recovered; tax not yet rebated (exempted) shall no longer be processed." Based on this determination, the "Cooperation Agreement" had the illegal purpose of obtaining export tax rebates for a business that should not apply for export tax rebates, and therefore should be void.

Given that most of the contractual obligations stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement" of this case have been performed, and the domestic and foreign trade transactions involving third parties have been substantially completed, after the "Cooperation Agreement" is legally determined to be void, there will be no legal effect of restitution. However, considering the "Service Contract" signed by both parties and their statements in court, it is more appropriate to use the RMB 9,750,000 stipulated in the "Service Contract" as the standard for dividing interests between Minbao Company and Bochuang Company. After deducting the RMB 6,000,000 already paid by Minbao Company to Bochuang Company (the freight charges of over RMB 1,260,000 paid by Minbao Company should not be included), Minbao Company should pay an additional RMB 3,750,000. The export tax refund already obtained shall be handled in accordance with relevant administrative regulations.

The determination of the validity of the contract in this case by the court of first instance lacked legal basis and is corrected accordingly. Minbao Company's appeal request is partially supported. Bochuang Company's other claims are all dismissed. The court of second instance, in accordance with Articles 52(3) and 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 153(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. The first-instance judgment is reversed. 2. Minbao Company shall pay Bochuang Company RMB 3,750,000 within ten days after the judgment takes effect. 3. Bochuang Company's other claims are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 294,109 shall be borne by Bochuang Company in the amount of RMB 147,054.50 and by Minbao Company in the amount of RMB 147,054.50. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 274,351 shall be borne by Bochuang Company in the amount of RMB 137,175.50 and by Minbao Company in the amount of RMB 137,175.50.

Bochuang Company, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: 1. Considering the background and content of the signing of the "Cooperation Agreement," the "Cooperation Agreement" had no contractual purpose of outputting benefits from state-owned assets. The court of second instance, to achieve the purpose of finding the "Cooperation Agreement" void, subjectively imposed this purpose on the contracting parties, which is inconsistent with the facts. It was precisely based on the allocation of rights and obligations under the contract that Bochuang Company and Minbao Company agreed in the agreement that Minbao Company would only charge a management fee of 0.6%. This allocation of interests is commensurate with the obligations assumed by both parties in the import and export project involved, conforming to the principle of reciprocity of rights and obligations. The difference in income between the two parties is mainly because Bochuang Company had to pay a large number of expenses, including hiring dozens of foreign experts and technical engineers, executing a large amount of specific and tedious work, and assuming the main project risks, such as quality and after-sales service, while Minbao Company's income was fixed and risk-free, and the export performance entirely belonged to Minbao Company, which was Minbao Company's main purpose. The second-instance judgment's finding that Minbao Company's benefit was disproportionate to the huge contractual risks it assumed was inconsistent with the facts and lacked evidence. 2. The "Contract Agreement" stipulated that after Minbao Company received the export tax refund, it would pay the entire export tax refund to Bochuang Company within five working days. This stipulation is not illegal. After the export tax refund entered Minbao Company's account, it ceased to be an export tax refund and became project income. The agreement that the tax refund obtained by Minbao Company from the export of goods should belong to Bochuang Company was a redistribution of income after the parties cooperated in exporting the goods. This stipulation is an act of Minbao Company disposing of its own lawful property according to its own will and an act of exercising its enterprise autonomy. This act falls within the scope of civil and commercial property disposition in the private law field and is not within the scope of tax law adjustment. In this case, there was no illegal act of fraudulently obtaining national export tax rebates. The facts of this case also show that during the cooperation between Minbao Company and Bochuang Company, Bochuang Company did not become the subject of the tax refund. In the process of tax refund, Minbao Company always conducted and completed it in its own name. At the same time, there was no malicious collusion between the parties to harm the interests of the state, the collective, or third parties. The second-instance judgment confused the boundary between the subject of the tax refund and how the subject disposes of the tax refund after receiving it. From the background of the cooperation between the parties in this case and the actual performance of the contract, there was no situation of obtaining export tax rebates for a business that should not apply for export tax rebates. The export business in this case actually existed. Minbao Company actually participated in the entire process of the export business in this case. The sales contract it concluded with the foreign party and the export product procurement contract it concluded with the domestic manufacturer have both been actually fully performed. The export business in this case was not completed by Bochuang Company operating under the guise of Minbao Company's name. Instead, both parties jointly formed a special team to cooperate and complete it together. The second-instance judgment, based on Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the 'Notice of the State Administration of Taxation and the Ministry of Commerce on Further Standardizing the Order of Foreign Trade Export Operations and Effectively Strengthening the Administration of Export Goods Tax Rebates (Exemptions)' (Guo Shui Fa [2006] No. 24), determined that the "Cooperation Agreement" was void because it had the illegal purpose of obtaining export tax rebates for a business that should not apply for export tax rebates. This is an error in the application of law. 3. After finding the "Cooperation Agreement" void, the court of second instance divided the rights and obligations of the parties based on the "Service Contract." This judgment result contradicts its determination of the validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" and violates legal provisions. In this case, the "Service Contract" was signed by the parties on March 15, 2007. This contract only stipulated that Minbao Company commissioned Bochuang Company to redesign and supervise the manufacture of the drilling rig's moving track and control system, with a contract amount of RMB 9,750,000. The purpose of signing this contract was to present it to Minsheng Bank so that Minbao Company could pay the difference payment to Bochuang Company within the validity period of the advance payment guarantee. This contract did not substantially modify the content of the "Cooperation Agreement." At most, it was a supplement to the supervision obligations that Bochuang Company should perform under the "Cooperation Agreement," and did not reflect all the rights and obligations of both parties. The second-instance judgment's determination of the rights and obligations of the parties based on the "Service Contract" is inconsistent with the facts. Moreover, Bochuang Company never requested Minbao Company to pay the price according to the "Service Contract" in its claims. The second-instance judgment exceeded the claims. Therefore, it requested: to reverse the second-instance judgment; to modify the judgment to order Minbao Company to pay Bochuang Company the contract arrears of RMB 48,770,061.62 and interest on the principal of RMB 10,113,120.06 at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period from April 16, 2008, to the actual date of payment; and the litigation costs shall be borne by Minbao Company.

The respondent, Minbao Company, argued in its defense for the retrial: 1. The purpose of the "Cooperation Agreement" was that Bochuang Company attempted to export under the guise of Minbao Company's name to obtain huge export tax refund benefits by using Minbao Company as a shell. From the content of the "Cooperation Agreement," it includes two parts. First, to solve Bochuang Company's status and interests, Bochuang Company attempted to operate export activities under the guise of Minbao Company's name and obtain export benefits by controlling Minbao Company. Second, to deal with domestic and foreign manufacturers and the national import and export tax refund management system, it arranged for Minbao Company to sign domestic and foreign trade contracts with domestic and foreign trade manufacturers and handle procurement, storage, export tax refunds, etc. In this activity, Minbao Company only obtained 0.6% of the benefits, while the remaining benefits all belonged to Bochuang Company. The purpose of the "Cooperation Agreement" was that Bochuang Company attempted to engage in export trade activities under a borrowed name to obtain huge export tax refund benefits by using a shell. The "Cooperation Agreement" in this case is void due to its illegal purpose. The second-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. This determination also reflects the opinion of the State Administration of Taxation. 2. The parties' disposition of civil rights and interests must also comply with legal provisions and be limited to civil interests obtained from lawful activities; otherwise, the distribution agreement is void. Therefore, the agreement in the "Cooperation Agreement" that Bochuang Company would obtain trade benefits and export tax refund benefits should not be protected by law. 3. Minbao Company actually signed and performed the domestic and foreign trade contracts and actually assumed all risks and responsibilities under those contracts. Although the "Cooperation Agreement" overlaps with the content of the domestic and foreign trade contracts in signing and performance, they are independent and should not be conflated. Therefore, the invalidity of the "Cooperation Agreement" due to illegality does not affect the validity of the domestic and foreign trade contracts, which should be protected by law. 4. Minbao Company obtained two types of benefits from operating the domestic and foreign trade business: first, the trade margin; second, the export tax refund. Neither of these benefits is property obtained from a void contract. The result of the second-instance judgment complies with Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and does not exceed the claims. The "Cooperation Agreement" is void due to illegality, for which both parties are at fault. The court of second instance appropriately used the "Service Contract," which had not yet been fully performed by both parties, as the standard for allocating responsibility between the parties. There is no impropriety. In conclusion, it requests the dismissal of Bochuang Company's application for retrial.

Both parties have no objection to the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, and this Court confirms them.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute in this case are: first, how should the validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" involved in this case be determined? Second, how should the export tax refund obtained by Minbao Company be handled?

I. Regarding the Validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" Involved in This Case.

BoChuang Company and Minbao Company explicitly stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement" signed between them that they would jointly export drilling equipment, with Minbao Company responsible for signing and executing foreign trade contracts and domestic procurement contracts; however, the foreign trade contracts and domestic procurement contracts would directly bind BoChuang Company and the foreign customer, and BoChuang Company and the domestic supplier, and Minbao Company would charge a management fee of 0.6% of the total amount of the foreign trade contracts. In terms of its content, the Agreement is a typical foreign trade agency contract. The revised Foreign Trade Law of the People's Republic of China, effective July 1, 2004, abolished the foreign trade licensing system and expanded the scope of "foreign trade operators." Article 8 of that Law provides that foreign trade operators "refer to legal persons, other organizations, or individuals that have gone through industrial and commercial registration or other practicing procedures in accordance with the law and engage in foreign trade business activities in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws and administrative regulations"; Article 12 provides that "foreign trade operators may accept the entrustment of others and conduct foreign trade business on their behalf within their business scope." The "Cooperation Agreement" represents the true intention of both parties, and its content does not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws or administrative regulations; therefore, it should be held valid.

The judgment of the second instance held that the "Cooperation Agreement" was invalid primarily based on two grounds: first, the purpose of the "Cooperation Agreement" concerning the export of benefits from state-owned assets was illegal; second, the "Cooperation Agreement" had the illegal purpose of obtaining export tax rebates for transactions that were not eligible to apply for and obtain export tax rebates. Regarding the issue of benefit export harming the legitimate rights and interests of state-owned assets, the content of the "Cooperation Agreement" was that BoChuang Company would organize sources of goods, procure export products, and finalize sales with the foreign customer, but would enter into domestic procurement contracts and foreign export contracts under the name of Minbao Company. This form of trade does not violate the provisions of Chinese laws or administrative regulations and does not constitute a situation of concealing illegal purposes in a lawful form as stipulated in the Contract Law. The parties' agreement on rights, obligations, and distribution of benefits in the corresponding export trade through the "Cooperation Agreement" is their true intent. The judgment of the second instance held that most of the benefits accrued to BoChuang Company, thus finding an imbalance of interests and further determining that it harmed the interests of state-owned assets; this lacks factual and legal basis. Regarding the issue of export tax rebates: the foreign trade contract under the export transactions involved in this case was actually performed and has been fully performed, with genuine export of goods. The entity entitled to the tax rebate is Minbao Company, which signed the export trade contract with the foreign customer. Minbao Company's receipt of the export tax rebate complies with Chinese laws and administrative regulations. The "Cooperation Agreement" stipulates that after Minbao Company receives the export tax rebate under the foreign trade contract, it must pay the full amount of the tax rebate to BoChuang Company within five banking days. This is an agreement between the parties for the redistribution of the export tax rebate lawfully obtained by Minbao Company, reflecting the true intent of the parties, and Minbao Company has the right to dispose of this sum. Export tax rebates are a measure adopted by China to encourage exports. In this case, there is no situation of falsely claiming exports without actual goods being exported; it is not a case of defrauding the state of export tax rebates. During the second instance trial, the court of second instance sought the opinion of the State Administration of Taxation, but the State Administration of Taxation only provided its understanding of the interpretation of paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the "Notice on Further Regulating the Order of Foreign Trade Export Operations and Effectively Strengthening the Administration of Export Goods Tax Rebates (Exemptions)" jointly issued by the State Administration of Taxation and the Ministry of Commerce, without making a determination on the validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" in dispute in this case. The "Notice on Further Regulating the Order of Foreign Trade Export Operations and Effectively Strengthening the Administration of Export Goods Tax Rebates (Exemptions)" is not an administrative regulation. If the conduct of Minbao Company and BoChuang Company violated its provisions, whether and how to impose administrative penalties is an administrative function of the competent authorities, not within the scope of trial in this case. Therefore, the "Cooperation Agreement" is not a contract signed for the illegal purpose of defrauding the state of export tax rebates.

In summary, the "Cooperation Agreement" in this case does not fall under any of the circumstances set forth in Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. The court of second instance erred in finding the "Cooperation Agreement" invalid, as there is no factual or legal basis for such a finding, and this should be corrected. BoChuang Company's grounds for retrial regarding the validity of the "Cooperation Agreement" are well-founded and should be supported.

II. Regarding the treatment of the export tax rebates involved in this case.

Since the "Cooperation Agreement" is valid, both parties should perform their contractual obligations in accordance with the agreement. Article 5 of the "Cooperation Agreement" clearly stipulates that after Minbao Company receives the export tax rebate under the foreign trade contract, it must pay the full amount of the tax rebate to BoChuang Company within five banking days. Accordingly, Minbao Company should pay the export tax rebate of RMB 38,458,237.51 to BoChuang Company. The judgment of the second instance, which stated that "the export tax rebate already obtained should be handled in accordance with relevant administrative regulations," is inappropriate and should be corrected. Minbao Company's claim that the export transactions in this case were conducted by it on its own account is not supported because Minbao Company failed to provide sufficient evidence. Given that BoChuang Company did not appeal and accepted the result of the first instance judgment, i.e., deducting RMB 1,800,000 from the export tax rebate of RMB 38,458,237.51 as Minbao Company's service compensation, Minbao Company should pay BoChuang Company RMB 36,658,237.51. This Court confirms this.

Furthermore, Minbao Company should, in accordance with Article 4 of the "Cooperation Agreement," pay to BoChuang Company the price difference obtained after performance of the domestic and foreign trade contracts, after deducting relevant costs and expenses and its due management fee. Regarding this, BoChuang Company expressly indicated its acceptance of the amount confirmed by the first instance judgment, i.e., RMB 9,852,037.93, and no longer insisted on its claim of RMB 10,113,120.06. This Court confirms this. Minbao Company argued that the "Cooperation Agreement" was not actually performed and that what was actually performed between it and BoChuang Company was the "Service Contract," and that the judgment of the second instance, which determined Minbao Company's payment to BoChuang Company based on the "Service Contract," was reasonable. Considering the content of the "Service Contract" and the subsequent "Supplementary Agreement," as well as the actual circumstances of the performance of the domestic and foreign trade contracts in this case, BoChuang Company's explanation for the execution of the "Service Contract" and the subsequent "Supplementary Agreement" is more persuasive: the parties signed the "Service Contract" so that BoChuang Company could obtain funds under the advance payment guarantee in advance to fulfill its obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement." The "Service Contract" was not actually performed; therefore, the RMB 9,750,000 under the "Service Contract" should not be used as the basis for determining Minbao Company's payment to BoChuang Company. The judgment of the second instance, which determined Minbao Company's payable amount to BoChuang Company based on the "Service Contract," is inappropriate and should be corrected.

In conclusion, the first instance judgment found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and reached the appropriate result; it should be affirmed. The second instance judgment found the facts clearly but applied the law incorrectly, and should be corrected. BoChuang Company's grounds for retrial are well-founded, and its claims should be supported. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, subparagraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby orders as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2011) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 854 of the Beijing High People's Court;

2. Affirm the civil judgment (2010) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 1940 of the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court.

Court acceptance fees for the first instance shall be borne as determined in the first instance judgment; court acceptance fees for the second instance, in the amount of RMB 274,351, shall be borne by China Poly Minbao Technology Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
